title: Not All Nudges Land: Behavioral Controllability and Elaboration Quality in AI-Supported Journaling
abstract: arXiv:2608.12582v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI journaling tools can tailor prompts to a person's own sensed behavior, but it is unclear which behaviors respond to them. We analyzed 369 journal entries from an eight-week passive sensing study. An LLM labeled each entry as expressing an intention to change a behavior or not, and we measured follow-through against 26 sensor features with a 3-day before/after comparison. Responsiveness depended most on whether a behavior involves other people. Behaviors that depend on others improved in only 15 to 22% of cases, while behaviors a person can act on alone improved more often, up to 50 to 63%, though unevenly. How users wrote mattered less. No single text feature separated improved from unimproved entries; writing carried signal only within specific behaviors, most clearly for text messaging and for longer, more personal intention entries. translated_title: 并非所有提示都能奏效：AI辅助日记中的行为可控性与阐述质量
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.12582v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：AI日记工具可以根据个人感知到的行为定制提示，但哪些行为会对此产生响应尚不清楚。我们分析了一项为期八周的被动感知研究中的369篇日记条目。一个大型语言模型将每个条目标记为是否表达了改变行为的意图，并通过26个传感器特征，采用3天前后对比来衡量后续执行情况。响应性最取决于行为是否涉及他人。依赖他人的行为仅在15%至22%的案例中有所改善，而个人可以独立行动的行为改善频率更高，可达50%至63%，尽管分布不均。用户的写作方式影响较小。没有任何单一文本特征能区分改善与未改善的条目；写作仅在特定行为中携带信号，最明显的是短信以及更长、更个人化的意图条目。样本量较小，因此我们将这些视为探索性模式，指向AI日记可能发挥作用的领域。
tldr: 本研究发现，AI日记提示的效果主要取决于行为是否依赖他人，个人可控行为更易改善，而写作质量的影响相对有限。
en_tdlr: This study finds that the effectiveness of AI journaling prompts depends primarily on whether behaviors rely on others, with personally controllable behaviors showing greater improvement, while writing quality has limited impact.
